chapter: Chicago, Ohio and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Ohio: the job in Ada, meeting his wife in Lima and the Mills Brothers
summary: After Cleveland he plays a frat-house job in Ada, Ohio, meets his future wife in Lima, joins his first union and meets the Mills Brothers.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well, then Jelly, he started to move around. But I was...I left Chicago... Wait a minute, now. There's
Thomas - 54
another time that messed with my life. I left Chicago and went to Cleveland, but I didn't stay in Cleveland somehow... Somehow, we got a job in a little town called Ada, Ohio.
Ada?

Yeah. It was a school town. So they put us up in one of the frat houses. And we got twenty dollars a week and a room. But we used to put five dollars apiece in, and we eat off of that five dollars... There was four of us; four or five of us. We could eat off that five dollars during the week. We did our own laundry. We washed and ironed our own shirts and things. That's how I first got involved with that cooking thing, you know, because we used to... We had everybody put their little two cents in and cook. And then that's where I met my wife, you know. My wife was from Lima, and Lima was the closest town to Ada.
Your wife is from Ohio, too, huh?

Yeah, my wife is from Lima. So we went in Lima, and we met all the little girls, and I picked my wife out. I picked her out of all the other girls. And some people there say...though that I went with somebody, but I didn't fool with nobody but her. And that's how we got close.
And then we played with some guy, I don't know where he come from, a guy who had a car -- and he played a lot of the
Thomas - 55
resorts down there. There was a lot of resorts in Ohio. And we made our Sunday gigs with him... Because that's how I met the Mills Brothers. See, the Mills Brothers are from Ohio; they was from...
Where did you meet them?
In a town over there, what the heck did they call it...? A little town.
Sandusky?
No. A little town south of Lima. It was a resort.
A resort?
And the first union I joined was in Ohio. It was Springfield. And that's where I ran into the Mills Brothers, in ...(?)... We've been great friends for years.
You act like you've played some ...(?)...
Yeah. Well, we done that thing in (?).
It's funny. I mean, you meeting them.

Yeah. I first met them in Ohio. And when they come... They got to New York before we did; they was popular. I met the guy (I can't think of his name) that used to arrange for the Mills Brothers. But he wasn't no band arranger or nothin'; you know, from what I knew. Because I had sense enough to know then he had too many notes in that thing, it just didn't make no kinda sense.
